Back when I first started I jumped into mining before I started another character to run security missions with.

Thanks for the welcome :) Now at the start I have started with mining, and I will continue with it as I feel now, when I have gotten my feet more wet and know more of the game I will maybe run another character for something else.

I have always played "gathering" characters in any MMO so for me mining is more of a safe place to begin while I still new. Fly safe you too!

Mining is alright when you're new, it's a fine way to ease into the game. In the long run though, you'll probably find that you really can't go anywhere with it - you can buy bigger ships and get bigger yields, but at no point does your gameplay experience change or improve as you advance in a mining career path - shooting rocks is pretty much shooting rocks.

PvP in it's various forms is where EVE really excels. I'd recommend that you make shooting people in the face a top priority in the short term. The least frustrating way to do that as a newbie is to get in a corporation that runs new player friendly fleets. I'd personally recommend EVE University to anyone, but there are many other fine options out there as well. There's even some rumors of a Voat corp forming in the near future...

Mining is useful to establish your own personal economy but another great way is to check out the Sisters of Eve The Blood-Stained Stars epic mission arc. It will introduce you to combat better and give you skillbooks and your first cruiser.

Google builds a profile based on everything you search for. Your future search results are based on your previous searches.

Try this: Search for something random on Google; the less specific the better. Then have a friend elsewhere do that search using the exact same terms at the same time, and watch how the results change. For instance if you search for a current event that everyone's reporting on and are a regular at Fox News, you will likely get hits from those pages first.
